proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord / magic_item kind
proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord has no magic_item variant. The taxonomy has magic_item_root as a source atom and the unit kind is tagged magic_item, but types.ts only defines SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord. No family (attunement, single-use consumption, passive property, etc.) exists for magic items at all.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Manual of Gainful Exercise is a Wondrous Item — neither a spell, class feature, nor mastery.

proposed_widenings.name: downtime_ritual activation cost
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's activation requires 48 hours of study/practice over 6 days or fewer — a downtime-duration cost. ClassFeatureActivationCost only covers 'free' and 'bonus_action'; CastingTime.minutes covers long casts but is spell-scoped. No variant covers multi-day downtime rituals.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines…

proposed_widenings.name: modify_ability_score (permanent)
proposed_widenings.justification: The core effect is a permanent +2 to the Strength ability score (capped at 30). No effect atom covers permanent ability-score modification. TAXONOMY v4 §12 explicitly lists 'modify_ability_score as a runtime effect' as out-of-scope / not promoted. This unit forces the question of whether permanent stat increases from magic items should be modeled.
proposed_widenings.evidence: your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 30

proposed_widenings.name: item_depletion with timed_recharge lifecycle
proposed_widenings.justification: After use, the item loses its magic entirely and regains it only after 100 years. This is a one-use depletion + century-scale recharge — distinct from charge-based resources (which refill on rest) and from spell slot consumption. No lifecycle atom or resource variant covers this pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The manual then loses its magic but regains it in a century.

notes: The blocking gap is structural: UnitRecord has no magic_item kind and no MagicItemMechanics family. Even if the kind existed, the core effect (permanent ability score increase) is explicitly listed in TAXONOMY v4 §12 as out-of-scope for the core mechanics graph. The activation cost (multi-day downtime ritual) and depletion/recharge lifecycle also lack surface representation. No honest encoding is possible without first landing MagicItemRecord in types.ts.
